items.followUp: Explain how transpiration helps water move from roots to leaves.

rubric.why: Identifies the pull or tension produced by transpiration.
rubric.description: Transpiration creates a pulling force (tension).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that transpiration creates a pull or tension.

rubric.why: States what the pull moves and its direction or pathway.
rubric.description: This force draws water upward through the xylem from roots to leaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the upward movement of water through xylem.

modelAnswer: Transpirational pull is the force or tension produced by transpiration from leaves.
It pulls water upward through the xylem from roots to leaves.

items.followUp: Define pulmonary circulation and state the route taken by blood in it.

rubric.why: Gives the route of blood through the lungs.
rubric.description: Pulmonary circulation carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct heart-to-lungs-to-heart route.

rubric.why: Gives the route of blood through the body.
rubric.description: Systemic circulation carries blood from the left ventricle to the body and back to the right atrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct heart-to-body-to-heart route.

modelAnswer: Pulmonary circulation is the circulation of blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium.
Systemic circulation is the circulation of blood from the left ventricle to the body and back to the right atrium.

items.followUp: Name the three major divisions of Biology and describe what each studies.

rubric.why: Gives the meaning of Biology.
rubric.description: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining Biology as the study of living things.

rubric.why: Identifies the division dealing with plants.
rubric.description: Botany is the study of plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Botany and its subject.

rubric.why: Identifies the division dealing with animals.
rubric.description: Zoology is the study of animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Zoology and its subject.

rubric.why: Identifies the division dealing with microorganisms.
rubric.description: Microbiology is the study of microorganisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Microbiology and its subject.

modelAnswer: Biology is the scientific study of living organisms.
Botany is the study of plants.
Zoology is the study of animals.
Microbiology is the study of microorganisms.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell wall and state two of its functions.

rubric.why: Identifies the membrane as the cell's surrounding boundary.
rubric.description: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible boundary around the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its position and general structure.

rubric.why: Describes the membrane's basic molecular structure.
rubric.description: It consists mainly of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the phospholipid bilayer and embedded proteins.

rubric.why: States the key property that permits controlled exchange.
rubric.description: The membrane is selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying selective permeability.

rubric.why: Explains the membrane's control of exchange.
rubric.description: It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for controlled movement across the membrane.

rubric.why: States another important function of the membrane.
rubric.description: It separates the cell contents from the external environment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the separating or protective function.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible boundary surrounding the cell.
It is made mainly of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
It is selectively permeable.
It controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.
It separates the cell contents from the external environment.

items.followUp: What is an enzyme? Explain how temperature can affect its activity.

rubric.why: Identifies enzymes as biological catalysts.
rubric.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining enzymes as biological catalysts.

rubric.why: States the effect of enzymes on reactions.
rubric.description: They speed up biochemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for their effect on reaction rate.

rubric.why: Recognises enzyme specificity.
rubric.description: Each enzyme acts on a particular substrate or type of reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are specific.

rubric.why: Gives a further characteristic of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are not used up in reactions; their activity depends on conditions such as temperature and pH, and high temperature can denature them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid characteristic such as being unchanged after the reaction or having an optimum condition/being denatured by high temperature.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are not used up in the reactions they catalyse.
Each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature and pH; high temperature can denature it.

items.followUp: Define anaerobic respiration and describe one industrial use of it.

rubric.why: Defines fermentation as the breakdown of glucose without oxygen.
rubric.description: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose by microorganisms or their enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for glucose breakdown and 1 mark for the absence of oxygen.

rubric.why: Identifies the products of yeast fermentation.
rubric.description: Yeast fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming these products.

rubric.why: Gives a practical use of fermentation.
rubric.description: Fermentation is used in food production, such as bread making, and in producing alcohol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct application.

rubric.why: Explains its wider importance.
rubric.description: Fermentation is important in producing useful food products and other products on a large scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a further valid statement of importance.

modelAnswer: Fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose by microorganisms or their enzymes.
In yeast, fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide and releases a small amount of energy.
Fermentation is used in bread making; carbon dioxide makes the dough rise.
It is also used to produce alcoholic beverages.
Fermentation is important in making useful food and industrial products.

items.followUp: State how nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in fertilizers help crops grow.

rubric.why: States that fertilizers supply nutrients needed by plants.
rubric.description: Fertilizers supply essential mineral nutrients to plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for supplying essential plant nutrients.

rubric.why: Names the main nutrients commonly supplied by fertilizers.
rubric.description: They commonly supply nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the three major nutrients.

rubric.why: Explains how fertilizers improve or restore soil nutrient levels.
rubric.description: They increase soil fertility by replenishing mineral nutrients.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for improving soil fertility or replenishing nutrients.

rubric.why: Connects fertilizer use with crop growth or production.
rubric.description: They promote plant growth and can increase crop yield.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for improved growth or yield.

modelAnswer: Fertilizers supply essential mineral nutrients to plants.
They commonly provide nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
They replenish nutrients in the soil and improve its fertility.
This promotes plant growth and increases crop yield.

items.followUp: Compare the structure of arteries and veins and state the direction in which each carries blood.

rubric.why: States the direction of blood flow in arteries.
rubric.description: Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction.

rubric.why: Describes the strong artery wall.
rubric.description: Arteries have thick, elastic, muscular walls to withstand high pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the thick, elastic or muscular walls.

rubric.why: Gives a further structural or functional feature of arteries.
rubric.description: Arteries have a relatively narrow lumen and carry blood under high pressure; their expansion can be felt as a pulse.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct additional feature.

rubric.why: Adds a valid qualification or feature of arteries.
rubric.description: Arterial blood is usually oxygenated, except in the pulmonary artery; arteries generally lack valves along their length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct exception or valve feature.

rubric.why: Describes how arteries distribute blood through the body.
rubric.description: Arteries branch into smaller arterioles that distribute blood to body tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the branching or distribution function.

modelAnswer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart to the body organs.
They have thick, muscular and elastic walls to withstand the high pressure of blood.
Their lumen is relatively narrow, and the rhythmic expansion of an artery can be felt as a pulse.
Arterial blood is usually oxygenated; the pulmonary artery is an exception.
Arteries branch into smaller arterioles that distribute blood to the tissues.
